statement: Know whether each drug the firm makes or repackages is a penicillin drug (trade names can differ by region and country).
quote: Manufacturers, including repackers, are responsible for knowing whether their drug is penicillin.

statement: Penicillin finished-drug manufacturers, including repackers, establish a comprehensive control strategy designed to prevent other drugs being cross-contaminated with penicillin.
quote: all penicillin finished pharmaceutical manufacturers, including repackers, are required by the CGMP regulations to establish a comprehensive control strategy designed to prevent cross-contamination of other drugs with penicillin
condition: penicillin finished drug manufacture or repacking

statement: As part of the penicillin cross-contamination control strategy of a finished-drug manufacturer or repacker, keep penicillin facilities and equipment separate.
quote: 21 CFR 211.42(d): Separation of facility and equipment
condition: penicillin finished drug manufacture or repacking

statement: As part of the penicillin cross-contamination control strategy of a finished-drug manufacturer or repacker, use separate air handling (HVAC) systems for penicillin.
condition: penicillin finished drug manufacture or repacking

statement: As part of the penicillin cross-contamination control strategy of a finished-drug manufacturer or repacker, test products for traces of penicillin where possible exposure exists.
quote: 21 CFR 211.176: Test for traces of penicillin where possible exposure exists.

statement: Manufacture penicillin active pharmaceutical ingredients under CGMP.
quote: Penicillin active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) are also required to be manufactured under CGMP

statement: API manufacturers, including those that make or package APIs or penicillin intermediates, take actions to keep penicillin material contained so it does not contaminate other drugs.
quote: API manufacturers, including those that manufacture or package APIs or penicillin intermediates, should follow to ensure such material is contained and does not contaminate other drugs

statement: Take precautions to prevent the use of wood products treated with or exposed to a halogenated phenolic preservative anywhere in the supply chain, including in every facility that makes, holds or distributes drug products, components or packaging materials.
quote: FDA recommends that manufacturers and distributors take precautions to prevent the use of wood products treated with or exposed to a halogenated phenolic preservative anywhere in the supply chain. This includes all facilities that manufacture, hold, or distribute drug products, components, or packaging materials.

statement: Do not store drug products, components or packaging materials near wood or wood-derived storage materials unless there is assurance that the wood has not been treated with a halogenated phenolic preservative.
quote: We recommend that manufacturers not store drug products, components, or packaging materials near wood or wood-derived storage materials unless there is assurance that the wood material has not been treated with a halogenated phenolic preservative.
condition: unless assurance the wood is untreated

statement: Set up agreements with suppliers and ask them for certification giving assurance that halogenated phenolic preservatives are not present.
quote: FDA further recommends that manufacturers establish agreements and request certification from suppliers to provide assurance that halogenated phenolic preservatives are not present.

statement: Stay alert to the characteristic odor of halogenated anisole compounds so the firm can intervene before products are contaminated or further distributed.
quote: Manufacturers should also be vigilant to the characteristic odor of the offending compounds so they can intervene before products are contaminated or further distributed.

statement: Prevent contamination of drug products with halogenated anisole compounds by following CGMP, rather than relying on detection methods.
quote: FDA expects that manufacturers prevent such contamination through adherence to CGMP

statement: Obtain assurances from suppliers and take measures to prevent exposure to problematic compounds such as halogenated anisoles, as part of a CGMP-compliant quality system.
quote: A CGMP-compliant quality system will ensure that assurances are obtained from suppliers and that measures are taken to prevent exposure to problematic compounds.

statement: Finished-drug manufacturers have written sanitation procedures designed to prevent contamination of equipment, components, drug product containers, closures, packaging, labeling materials and drug products.
quote: the CGMP regulations at 21 CFR 211.56(c) require written procedures for sanitation designed to prevent the contamination of equipment, components, drug product containers, closures, packaging, labeling materials, and drug products
